> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json aef631b80b3175f2f43287a6e0185c828c356ac8` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a200cfbda34f98cd236de0d10e5d937bd570f9c6` — the merge of head `41272f9f5693500d15a712731557f41502a8d982` into base `aef631b80b3175f2f43287a6e0185c828c356ac8`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a200cfbda34f98cd236de0d10e5d937bd570f9c6 && git checkout a200cfbda34f98cd236de0d10e5d937bd570f9c6
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin aef631b80b3175f2f43287a6e0185c828c356ac8 41272f9f5693500d15a712731557f41502a8d982 && git checkout -B drift-repro aef631b80b3175f2f43287a6e0185c828c356ac8 && git merge --no-ff 41272f9f5693500d15a712731557f41502a8d982

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json aef631b80b3175f2f43287a6e0185c828c356ac8
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs aef631b80b3175f2f43287a6e0185c828c356ac8` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `41272f9f5693500d15a712731557f41502a8d982`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/services/service-storage/src/storage-routes.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/storage-routes.test.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/chunked-upload-integrity.test.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/storage-limits.test.ts + packages/spec/src/api/storage.zod.ts (`GetPresignedUrlRequestSchema`, `InitiateChunkedUploadRequestSchema`, `UploadChunkRequestSchema`), packages/client/src/index.ts (`storage.upload`, `storage.uploadPart`, `storage.resumeUpload`), ui/packages/providers/src/UploadProvider.tsx (the presigned adapter), packages/services/service-storage/src/metadata-store.ts (`UploadSessionRecord.total_chunks`), packages/services/service-storage/src/objects/system-upload-session.object.ts (`total_chunks`), packages/types/src/response-envelope.ts (`sendError`). Face: narrowing, so the floor is every path of the diff outside the prose faces; the changeset is read under ② and is not reviewed under ④.

Inputs read: cards #27412 and #27413 with every comment (triage, claims, both `os-dev-report` comments, the seat's REWORK note); PR #27537 body, file list and the diff of its five files against the merge base `3604371f`; the 52 check-runs on `41272f9f`: 36 success, 16 skipped (UI, docs and opt-in lanes the paths do not select), 0 failed, 0 pending at the time of this record. `Check Changeset`, every `Lint` lane (the home of `check-adr-0087-registration` and `check-changeset-no-major`), `Test Core 1/8..8/8`, the type-check lanes, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` and `Dogfood Regression Gate` are among the 36.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Presigned door accept set for `size`.** Before: anything but `null`/`undefined`. Now: a JSON number that is finite and at least 0. Judged against the published `GetPresignedUrlRequestSchema.size` (`z.number()`): a string (numeric strings included) and a boolean were never inside the published set, so refusing them restores the contract and is not a narrowing: right. `NaN` is refused by `z.number()` itself, and no JSON wire body carries `NaN` or an infinity, so neither moves the published set over the wire: right. A negative number (`-5`, `-0.5`) IS inside the published set and is now refused: this is the one narrowing, and the PR body and changeset declare exactly it. Right. A fractional size stays accepted, which is what the spec declares today: consistent.
- **Chunk door accept set for `chunkIndex`.** Before: anything `parseInt` could read. Now: decimal digits, a safe integer, below the session's `total_chunks`. Judged against `UploadChunkRequestSchema.chunkIndex` (`z.number().int().min(0)`): `-1`, `0.5`, `1e0`, `0x0`, `abc` were never inside the published set, so the strict parse restores the contract: right. A whole number at or past `total_chunks` is inside the static schema (it has no upper bound the spec can state per session) but outside the protocol's declared capability: the init response declares `totalChunks` as the expected number of chunks, and the completion door has always refused a session holding a chunk beyond it, so no completable upload ever held one. Refusing it at the door where the harm is done is the right place, and it turns the completion door's refusal of such a session from a permanent 409 into a never-stored chunk. The `(narrowing)` arm the PR already carries covers the consumer-facing truth of this change whichever way a reader classifies it.
- **Public surface.** No route, export, type or error code is added, removed or renamed. `INVALID_REQUEST` is the code both doors already answer for a request they cannot take (the required-field refusals a few lines above each new check), and `details` is a declared field of the `sendError` envelope. The response shapes are unchanged. Right.
- **Refusal ordering.** Presigned: after the required-field check, before the scope gate, the limit and the `sys_file` insert. Chunk: after 404, the 403 resume-token check, the organization-reach check and the 410 expiry check, before a byte is read, stored or counted. This keeps the standing rule that a caller who cannot prove ownership learns nothing about the session, and the control test pins the 403-before-range order. Right.
- **Is narrowing below the published spec the right shape here, or should `size` be tightened in the spec?** The door narrowing is the right fix for these two cards: the route destructures `req.body` and never parses it with `GetPresignedUrlRequestSchema`, so a spec-only `.int().min(0)` would change nothing at runtime, and the 500 and the negative `sys_file` row would stay. Tightening the spec in THIS PR would be the wrong lane: `packages/spec` was outside the dispatched file surface, a spec edit owes regenerated api-surface and JSON-schema artifacts, and it would flip the review to the schema face in a spec-lane card. **Should-fix, as a spec-lane follow-up card (a recommendation, not filed here):** `GetPresignedUrlRequestSchema.size` to `.int().min(0)` with the presigned door moved to `Number.isInteger` in the same PR, so declared equals enforced in both directions; and in the same card, the init door, which `InitiateChunkedUploadRequestSchema` declares as `totalSize: int().min(1)` and `chunkSize: int().min(5242880)` while `POST /upload/chunked` checks `totalSize` only for truthiness (a negative `totalSize` mints a session with `total_chunks` of `-0` that no chunk can ever enter, and a numeric-string `totalSize` is stored as sent). That is a pre-existing hole in the same defect class as #27413; this PR does not touch it and does not worsen it (such a session could never complete before either).

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/27412-storage-route-input.md`: `'@objectstack/service-storage': patch`. The diff moves only that package; `packages/spec`, `packages/client` and `ui/` are untouched, so one bump is right.
- Declarations: `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` on both the PR body and the changeset, identical. The `Metadata-protocol` kind is right: nothing an author writes in metadata changes. Per the Post-Task Checklist, a non-protocol change that narrows ships `patch` and keeps its ADR-0087 disposition: the changeset carries exactly one marker, `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, whose reason matches the diff (no key, export, type or error code removed or renamed; nothing for `objectstack migrate meta` to rewrite; no tombstone owed). The `Narrowed:` sentence names the negative `size` against the spec's bare `z.number()`, which is the narrowing ① confirms.
- **Should-fix (prose, changeset):** the `Narrowed:` sentence could also name the whole-number `chunkIndex` at or past `total_chunks`, since `UploadChunkRequestSchema.chunkIndex` is `int().min(0)` with no upper bound; the body's "Exactly what is now refused" section already states it, so the disclosure exists and only the one-line summary is partial.
- The level gates on the head (`Check Changeset`, the `Lint` lanes) are green, which agrees with this reading.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev report 1 (comment 6495538727), `deviations`:
1. `storage-limits.test.ts` edited: inside the dispatch's "or a sibling test". The edit widens the session row to two declared chunks through `store.updateSession`, the real store write, and leaves the pinned claim (bytes across chunks against the limit) unchanged. Answered, holds.
2. Three commits, not two (now five after the patch round): history shape only; the branch is the identity and the queue merges the PR. Refusing a force-push was right. Answered.
3. Model-free commit trailers: the AGENTS.md form. Answered.
4. Worktree name differs between the two claims: cosmetic; one branch, one PR. Answered.
5. Package suite not rerun after the merge of `origin/main` at `3a10b29c`: superseded by `Test Core 1/8..8/8` green on `41272f9f`. Answered.
6. `os-dev-report` marker on the second line: `post-stamped` requires the signature first. Answered.

Dev report 2 (comment 6496406943), `deviations`:
7. An extra commit for the ADR-0087 marker: the gate requires it for the `(narrowing)` arm. Right.
8. PR body edit refused by the relay: the live body read for this record carries `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and the `Narrowed:` sentence, so the owed edit landed after that report. **Should-fix (prose, PR body):** the Acceptance note "three commits, not two" is stale (five); no gate reads it.

`open_questions`: empty in both reports. `out_of_scope_findings` (report 1): the spec `size` being `z.number()`: answered in ① with a follow-up recommendation. The dogfood battery the arm owes was run at `41272f9f` per report 2, and `Dogfood Regression Gate` is green on the head. The seat's REWORK note (comment 6495583454) asked for one item, the declaration; it is present on both carriers. No flag escalates.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/services/service-storage/src/storage-routes.ts`
- `isDeclaredByteCount`: `typeof === 'number'`, `Number.isFinite`, at least 0. Holds against the `sys_file` `size` number field and `requireWithinUploadLimit(size: number, ...)`: the former `Number(size)` coercion is gone, so a numeric string can no longer pass the limit check as a number and reach the insert as a string. `-0` passes (`-0 >= 0`) and is stored as `-0`, which serializes as `0`: harmless, noted. Tried: `""` is not `== null`, so it reaches this guard and is refused with the `size` message, which the test pins. Holds.
- `parseChunkIndex`: `/^\d+$/` (ASCII digits without the `u` flag) then `Number.isSafeInteger`. `"01"` reads as 1, a legal integer; an empty segment is caught by the `!chunkIndexStr` check above; an index past `MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` reads `null` and is refused. Holds.
- The range check reads `Number(session.total_chunks)`. `total_chunks` is `required: true` on `sys_upload_session`, typed `number` on `UploadSessionRecord`, and written unconditionally by the init door; the completion door already reads it with the same `Number(...)` (the `missingChunks`/`unexpectedChunks` judgment), so the two doors agree about one session, and a store that hands numerics back as strings is covered. Holds.
- Placement after `expireIfPastDeadline`: that helper writes the row only when the deadline has passed (`expiryStampDue(session) ? stampExpired(...) : session`), so a refused in-date chunk leaves the row untouched; the test pins `parts` and the progress unchanged. The check is a pure read before the conditional progress write, so the retry loop that door uses for progress is unaffected. Holds.
- Refusal envelope: `sendError(res, 400, 'INVALID_REQUEST', message, { details: { chunkIndex: raw, totalChunks } })`, with `details` a declared `extra` field. Echoing the raw segment (a string) is right for `abc`. The message picks `must be 0` for one chunk and `from 0 to N-1` otherwise; the N=2 case is pinned. Holds.
- Tried to break it: `total_chunks` of 0 or `-0` (reachable only through the init door's unvalidated `totalSize`, see ①): every index is refused with a truthful "declared 0 chunks" where before the chunk was stored and completion answered 409 for good; not a regression. A session without `total_chunks` cannot exist under the required field. A legitimate resume (`resumeUpload` iterates `uploadedChunks .. totalChunks-1` from the progress door) stays inside the range. Nothing breaks.

`packages/services/service-storage/src/storage-routes.test.ts`
- Eight refused sizes and two controls through the mounted handler, each asserting status, `error.code`, the message prefix and that `store.createFile` was never called; the controls read the stored row's `size` and `status`. `NaN` and `Infinity` are in-process-only inputs (JSON cannot carry them) and pin the predicate, not the wire. Holds against the scenario the card accepts (`"abc"`, `-5`, `NaN`, `""` each 400, no row; `0` and a positive size unchanged).

`packages/services/service-storage/src/chunked-upload-integrity.test.ts`
- Each of the seven refused indexes asserts status, code, message, `details`, no backend `uploadChunk` call, unchanged `parts` and progress, and then completes the same upload: the strongest pin of the card's "session that can never complete". The multi-chunk range message, the last declared index accepted, and 403-before-range are controls. The pre-existing stray-chunk completion case now plants the part on the session row, the shape a pre-fix session carries, so the completion door's `unexpectedChunks` branch stays reachable and covered instead of going dead. The reported ablation (range check removed: `1`, `7` and the multi-chunk case fail; the five non-digit cases stay refused by the strict parse) is consistent with what the suite can distinguish. Holds.

`packages/services/service-storage/src/storage-limits.test.ts`
- `declareTwoChunks` writes `total_chunks: 2` through `store.updateSession`, the same store the chunk door reads, so the fixture is honest and the two limit pins (413 on the chunk that crosses the limit; a retried index counted once) are unchanged in what they claim. Holds.

Findings: must-fix none. Should-fix: the spec-lane follow-up card in ① (size `.int().min(0)` with the door on `Number.isInteger`, plus the init door's `totalSize`/`chunkSize` enforcement); the `Narrowed:` sentence naming the out-of-range `chunkIndex` too (②); the stale "three commits" acceptance note (③).
